journal_lines: Good iron seam. Rust-orange in the wall.
Iron-bearing stone. Heavier than it looks.
Vein ran deeper than expected. Good.
Found the iron. Took the time to get it right.
Rust-stain in the rock where the iron sleeps. Woke a few of them.
Iron tastes like blood through the muzzle. The world remembers what it is made of.
A nodule the size of a small heart, almost. Took it gently.
Banded iron, layer on layer, every layer an old summer.
Struck the wall and the wall struck back. Sparks. Then iron.
The seam went where seams go. Followed it until it stopped.
Iron in the deep is patient. Patient about being found.
Took only what I could carry. The rest will keep.
